earnings.title: Permian Resources Announces Strong Third Quarter 2026 Results and Updated Full Year Guidance
highlights: Through the combination of higher prices and higher production volumes, Permian Resources’ total natural gas revenue increased by $141 million to $53 million during the quarter.
Similarly, the Company’s NGL revenue increased by $81 million quarter-over-quarter to $264 million.
Announced cash provided by operating activities of $1,255 million, cash capital expenditures of $518 million and adjusted free cash flow 1 of $846 million
Declared quarterly base dividend of $0.16 per share
Permian Resources generated third quarter net cash provided by operating activities of $1,255 million, adjusted operating cash flow 1 of $1,364 million and adjusted free cash flow 1 of $846 million.

quotes.text: This marks another outstanding quarter from the Permian Resources team, with continued execution across the board. During the third quarter, we responded to a strong price environment with higher production across all three commodity streams.
quotes.by: Will Hickey, Co-CEO of Permian Resources

quotes.text: Throughout the year our team has reacted quickly to higher commodity prices, growing production in order to maximize value for shareholders.
quotes.by: James Walter, Co-CEO of Permian Resources

outlook: Raised mid-point of full year guidance for oil production to 202.5 MBbls/d and updated mid-point of capital expenditures guidance to $2.025 billion

items.heading: Commodity prices are volatile, and a sustained period of low commodity prices for oil, NGLs and natural gas could adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.

If commodity prices decrease to a level such that our future undiscounted cash flows from our properties are less than their carrying value, we may be required to take write-downs of the carrying values of our properties.

Reserve estimates depend on many assumptions that may turn out to be inaccurate. Any material inaccuracies in reserve estimates or underlying assumptions will materially affect the quantities and present value of our reserves.
items.group: Risks Related to Our Reserves, Leases and Drilling Locations

items.heading: Unless we replace our reserves with new reserves and develop those reserves, our reserves and production will decline, which would adversely affect our future cash flows and results of operations.
items.group: Risks Related to Our Reserves, Leases and Drilling Locations

items.heading: The development of our estimated PUDs may take longer and may require higher levels of capital expenditures than we currently anticipate. Therefore, our estimated PUDs may not be ultimately developed or produced.
items.group: Risks Related to Our Reserves, Leases and Drilling Locations

items.heading: Certain of our undeveloped leasehold acreage is subject to leases that will expire over the next several years unless production is established on units containing the acreage, the primary term is extended through continuous drilling provisions or the leases are renewed.
items.group: Risks Related to Our Reserves, Leases and Drilling Locations
